NQ is quoted at 28,919.00, down 1.59%, holding near 7% of a 28,905.00 to 29,111.00 range after the bounce off the prior 28,942.50 low failed and a second consecutive hourly lower low printed. The DAX has rolled over to 25,431.09, down 0.54% in the lower quarter of its range, so Europe now confirms rather than contradicts, and the VIX is 17.67 against a 15.84 close. Against those two new amplifiers, Dow futures are down only 0.20%, the 10-year is unchanged at 4.97% with Treasury futures bid, and WTI is off its high inside an unchanged range. headline: NQ extends to a 28,905.00 low and the DAX rolls over to -0.54% near its own session low, adding a failed retracement and European confirmation, but YM at -0.20% and an unchanged 4.97% 10Y keep Tail inside the watch band at 23
body:
Two things changed in this hour and both of them cut the same way. NQ is quoted at 28,919.00, down 468.00 points or 1.59% against the 29,387.00 reference close, as of 04:16 EDT. The session low has extended from 28,942.50 to 28,905.00 and the range is now 28,905.00 to 29,111.00, a 206-point band, with the contract trading about 14 points off the low at roughly 7% of that range. The bounce attempted off the prior low failed and a second consecutive hourly lower low followed. That is repeated extension after a failed retracement, which is the single most relevant structure for a mean-reversion book, and it is the first time in this session that it has been observed.

The second change removes the counterweight that held the prior assessment down. One hour ago the DAX was quoted at 25,537.94, only 0.12% lower and trading near its session high, which argued that the first deep non-Asian pool was declining to extend the Asian de-rating. The DAX is now 25,431.09, down 137.47 points or 0.54%, inside a 25,391.91 to 25,548.78 range and sitting in the lower quarter of it. Europe has made a lower low and now confirms rather than contradicts. The VIX is quoted at 17.67 against a 15.84 close, up 11.56% and near the top of a narrow 17.48 to 17.81 range, with VIX futures also higher in delayed context.

What holds the score inside the watch band is that the move remains narrow and that the rate market refuses to join it. ES is 7,609.00, down 0.66%, and Dow futures are down about 0.20% against NQ's 1.59%. A 139 basis point spread between the Nasdaq and the Dow is the signature of a sector de-rating, not of index-wide liquidation, and it leaves the broad market with room to absorb the story. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.97%, essentially unchanged on the day and only marginally above the 4.95% H.15 print for 10 September, the 2-year is 4.63% against 4.56%, and Treasury futures across the 2s to 30s curve are modestly bid. In the historical failures of this strategy, aligned yields were present; here they are absent. WTI is 102.78, up 2.73%, but inside an unchanged 101.59 to 103.58 range and off its high, so the energy leg is consolidating rather than extending, and gold is lower in delayed context.

The catalyst stack behind the move is genuine and it is aligned. Over the weekend the chief executives of the two leading frontier AI laboratories argued publicly for slowing the pace of capability improvement, and the OpenAI chief executive said a public listing this year would be ill-advised, deferring it to 2027. Asia priced this first: the Nikkei closed 1.0% lower, Korea fell 3.2%, Asia-Pacific excluding Japan fell 1.1% and Chinese blue chips eased 0.5%. Separately, Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline, which had been carrying four to five million barrels a day as the primary alternative to a Strait of Hormuz that has been severely restricted since March, was shut after a drone attack on 11 September; Brent is now near 108.49 dollars, up 3.71%. Into that, market-implied odds of a quarter-point policy move at Wednesday's decision stand at 86 to 87%, up from roughly 70% before Friday's inflation data, and two major banks reversed their forecasts over the weekend.

Weighing the two new amplifiers against three intact counterweights, Tail moves two points to 23. That is inside the watch band and two points below the block threshold. The judgment is that a 206-point, 0.7% range built over fourteen hours with the Dow down 0.20% and the curve unmoved is not yet the path that denies mean reversion, even though its components are now pointing one way. Stress rises to 78 on the volatility, oil and policy stack, which is high but describes a recoverable environment rather than a structural break. Confidence holds at 88: live quotes for the index, European cash, volatility, oil and yields were obtained directly, every material story was verified at a primary or reputable source, and the only gaps are a partial shared cross-asset context file whose calendar section failed to collect and whose breadth and megacap sections describe the previous session rather than the current one.

Conditional risk stays concentrated in the 13:00 to 16:00 UTC window around the 13:30 UTC cash open, where the first American auction prices all three stories together. The conditional path peaks at Tail 25 in the first full cash hour, which maps to the block band for that single hour, and eases from 16:00 UTC. Nothing about that hour's structure is observed yet; 28,905.00 is the nearest conditional invalidation of the current band and a reclaim of 29,000 would be the first sign that two-way trade has returned.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours were available. Tail climbed steadily through the Sunday session from 10 at 08:00 UTC to 17 by 15:00 UTC, eased to 16, then stepped through 17, 18, 18 and 19 into the Globex reopen, crossing into the watch band at 21 and peaking at 22 in the reopen hour. Across the overnight session it was unusually stable, printing 20 in seven of the following nine hours with 19 at 02:00 and 06:00 UTC, before the European open lifted it to 21 at 07:00 UTC. The mapped state was EA_ON and green for the first 13 hours, then WATCH and yellow for most of the overnight session with two single-hour reversions to green. Dominant mode read normal through the Sunday hours, event/whipsaw for the reopen hour, and mixed for every hour since 23:00 UTC. Confidence fell from 86 to 71 around the 16:00 UTC handover, then rebuilt to 88 as live overnight price-path evidence accumulated.
outlookSummary: Conditional risk stays concentrated in the 13:00 to 16:00 UTC stretch around the 13:30 UTC cash open, the first American auction to price the weekend AI-pacing essays, the shut Saudi East-West pipeline and an implied 86 to 87% probability of a Wednesday policy move together. The forecast peaks at Tail 25 in the first full cash hour, the narrow single-hour top of the window, which is one point higher than the prior assessment projected because a failed retracement and European confirmation have since been observed. Through the remaining European hours conditional Tail holds at 23 and eases to 22 across the midday lull, with 28,905.00 as the nearest conditional invalidation and a reclaim of 29,000 as the first conditional sign of restored two-way trade. After 16:00 UTC the path decays through 22 and 21 into the cash close, drops to 19 and the EA_ON mapping across the maintenance break and the thin Globex and Asian hours, and rebuilds to 20 and then 21 as Europe reopens on the first day of the two-day policy meeting. Every value beyond the current clock hour is conditional risk, not observed structure.
